entries.body:
**Unofficial fork prerelease.** Based on upstream Actual v26.11.0 (`1766241e3f4b3c578e424c4fa15f1eb83c0da17d`, October 29, 2026); not an official Actual Budget release.

This release fixes the MCP server refusing every write. It also carries database and iPhone storage-safety work that changes how the web app and sync server start.
entries.details:
#### Features

- None in this release.

#### Enhancements

- None in this release.

#### Bugfixes

- The MCP server refused every write with "The loaded budget has no id" since the undo and audit change shipped, while reads kept working. Writes now work again (#508).
- A database migration and the record that it ran now commit as one transaction, so a migration that stops partway cannot leave the database half-migrated. This also repairs account types that an earlier migration left wrong (#502). **Affects the web app and the sync server Ken uses.**

#### Maintenance

- iPhone storage safety (off unless an iPhone shell turns it on, so web, desktop and the sync server behave as before): the page checks that each write reached storage before saying "Saved", shows storage status and notices, holds sync for writes that are not stored yet, flushes storage when the app goes to the background, and shows page alerts, confirms and prompts through the app (#473, #481 to #483, #485, #487, #490 to #493, #496, #498, #500, #501, #503 to #505). The `native/*` handlers in loot-core are gated and do nothing without a native shell. This build turns the guard on in the iPhone app source, but the iPhone app Ken uses does not get it until a new TestFlight build.
- Native reads now wait for the budget to open (#507). The Mac app reload now closes a page dialog (#506).
- iPhone app: it reloads its own page when the web process ends and tells the person (#484, #489); scheduled splits show the payee the web shows (#471, #472); Accounts amounts stay whole and search stays visible (#476); VoiceOver fixes (#479); the Undo button sits under its text at accessibility sizes (#504); notices wait for the Limits screen (#475).
- Specs, CI and tests: spec records for the storage work and Reconcile alert (#468, #469, #474, #478, #486, #488, #491, #495, #497), a release archive check that scans only compiled code (#477), and iPhone kill and UI test fixes (#480, #499).
- No upstream changes in this release; the fork stays on upstream Actual 26.11.0.

#### Known limitations

- Removing a deduction from a paycheck in the iPhone app can crash. The fix is tracked in sc-5504, and the next iPhone TestFlight build is held for it.
- Experimental.
- The native Schedules & Paychecks screens are off by default; turn them on in Settings to try them.
- Tapping a tag in the transaction editor does nothing.
- Tags are not yet fully accessible on the phone.
- OpenID sign-out needs the server's address in the identity provider's allowed sign-out addresses; without it the provider shows an error page, though you are already signed out of Actual.
- Attached documents aren't included in a budget export.
- Documents removed before alpha.35 are recorded the first time an updated device syncs, and deleted 30 days after that. Removals made on a device that has not been updated are not tracked.
- HEIC pictures are refused; use the Photos library or a JPEG or PNG copy.
- Attaching a document needs a connection; there is no offline upload queue.
- After restoring server data from a backup, pause the cleanup first (`production/RESTORE.md`).

This release changes how the hosted MCP server (the connector that lets Claude read and change a budget) decides what it may do: the permissions now come from a grants file instead of from which tools exist. Production's assistant can do everything except delete for now.

#### Features

- Every MCP entry now lists every tool, and each tool's description names the scopes it needs.
- The local (stdio) MCP entry takes its permissions from environment settings and stays read-only unless writes are turned on.

- The sync server deletes a document 30 days after a device first reports it removed from its transaction. Undoing the removal on any device, or opening the document, restarts the 30 days. A deleted budget's documents are deleted 30 days after the budget was deleted. A daily job does the deleting, at most 500 documents per run, and logs each deletion. Set `ACTUAL_ATTACHMENTS_ORPHAN_RETENTION_DAYS` to change the waiting period, or to `0` to stop all deletion.
- If you re-create a budget you deleted (upload it again under the same id), it keeps its documents and starts with no old shares.
- The server's `/metrics` shows how many bytes of documents are stored, how many are waiting to be deleted, and the result of the last cleanup.
- The hosted MCP server has a new `list_transaction_attachments` tool that lists a transaction's documents (metadata only; a split line lists its parent's). It treats attachment types and ids as untrusted.
- The iPhone app has a native Budget tab, behind a setting. You can edit a budgeted amount, step through months with arrows and a month menu, use tracking budgets (income Balance hidden, Saved or Overspent as on the web), and move money between categories and to-budget.

#### Enhancements

- Devices report removed and restored documents to the server when they sync.
- Pull down on the native Budget tab to sync, with a clear offline message when sync fails. The month menu knows the budget's range and puts a checkmark on the month you are viewing.
- The app has a new Home Economics icon, a jar of coins, on iPhone, Mac, Windows, Android and in the browser tab.
- The iPhone and Mac apps have a native look that follows the system's light and dark setting; the web app keeps its themes.
- The iPhone app uses the system tab bar for Budget, Accounts, Reports and Settings, with an Add button for new transactions and a light tap when you save a transaction or move money.
- In the iPhone app, attached documents open inside the app and can be saved to Photos, and signing out returns to the app's own sign-in screen.
- In the iPhone app, Back goes up one level, including on the Schedules list, and the phone layout holds in landscape.
- VoiceOver support on the native Budget screen, with an edit action on editable rows.
- The native bridge checks the page's origin before native code calls into it, so a foreign sign-in page can't be answered.

#### Bugfixes

- Changing the encryption key no longer fails when an attached document is missing from the server, and attached documents open again after another device changes the key.
- The desktop app removes the temporary copies of opened attachments when it quits.
- The iPhone and iPad app's content, and the iPad's top bar, stay clear of the status bar, camera cutout, rounded corners and home indicator.
- The iOS app launches when built with Xcode 27.

#### Maintenance

- No upstream changes in this release; the fork stays on upstream Actual 26.11.0.
- The hosted MCP server's dependencies `hono` and `@hono/node-server` are updated past security advisories.
- The rate-limit test is made tolerant of a loaded machine.
- Native iPhone and Mac app work and its OpenSpec records; the native app code itself affects iOS only.

#### Known limitations

- Experimental.
- Tapping a tag in the transaction editor does nothing.
- Tags are not yet fully accessible on the phone.
- OpenID sign-out needs the server's address in the identity provider's allowed sign-out addresses; without it the provider shows an error page, though you are already signed out of Actual.
- Attached documents aren't included in a budget export.
- Documents removed before this release are recorded the first time an updated device syncs, and deleted 30 days after that. Removals made on a device that has not been updated are not tracked.
- HEIC pictures are refused; use the Photos library or a JPEG or PNG copy.
- Attaching a document needs a connection; there is no offline upload queue.
- After restoring server data from a backup, pause the cleanup first (`production/RESTORE.md`).

This release lets a server owner require that the first OpenID sign-in is a named person, refuses an empty OpenID identity, and tightens the rate limits and start-up checks of the hosted MCP entry. The hosted MCP entry is still not deployed anywhere.
entries.details:
#### Features

- A new, optional setting, `ACTUAL_OPENID_ADMIN_SUBJECT`, names the provider subject (`sub`) that the first OpenID sign-in must have. When it is set, a first sign-in from any other identity is refused, so the first person to reach the sign-in page cannot become the administrator. Unset, the server behaves as upstream does: the first OpenID identity becomes the administrator, and the server logs a warning at start-up.
- The hosted MCP entry can serve a production host, read-only, but only when `ACTUAL_MCP_REMOTE_PRODUCTION=1` is set and the production guard is met: a session token file and no password, a provider subject (not an email address) as the allowed account, the data folder `production-remote`, and a token that belongs to a user who is not an administrator. Otherwise it still refuses a production host. It is not deployed anywhere yet.

#### Enhancements

- The hosted MCP entry limits its OAuth endpoints per source address and adds a ceiling over each /24 (IPv4) or /48 (IPv6) group of sources, set with `ACTUAL_MCP_RATE_PER_PREFIX` (default 600 per window). A request to `/mcp` with a valid token counts only against the per-client limit.
- The hosted MCP entry refuses to start with a loopback server address unless it also listens on loopback.
- The MCP image build leaves local `.env` files (`.env`, `.env.local` and `.env.*.local`) out of its build context.

#### Bugfixes

- The sync server now refuses an OpenID sign-in whose identity is empty. Upstream would have matched an empty identity to the password-method user. This fixes a flaw in upstream's code; it is fixed here only.
- When `ACTUAL_OPENID_ADMIN_SUBJECT` is set, the sync server also refuses a sign-in whose ID-token `sub` differs from the user-info `sub`.

#### Maintenance

entries.details:
#### Features

- An MCP server (`@actual-app/mcp`) lets an AI assistant that speaks the Model Context Protocol, such as Claude Code or Claude Desktop, look up accounts, categories, payees, transactions, budget months, schedules, paychecks and business calendars in your budget. It is **read-only by default**: it starts the budget engine read-only, so it sends nothing to the server. It talks to the assistant over standard input and output and opens no network port.
  - To install and run it, follow the "MCP Server" page in the API docs (`api/mcp-server`): build it from this release's tag with `yarn build:mcp`, keep the server password in 1Password and pass it with `op run`, and register the server with your assistant.
  - Changes are opt-in: a separate entry started with `--writes` adds tools to create transactions, change a transaction's category, payee or notes, set a budget amount, skip a paycheck and move an account on budget. Each change is recorded in a private audit log before it runs. `--writes` is never allowed for production.

- Descriptions read, for example, "2 business days before Payday (U.S. Federal Holidays)".
- Editing the other schedule or a business calendar updates relative schedules; undo restores both.
- If the other schedule is deleted, the relative schedule shows "Source schedule was deleted" until you choose another one or delete it.

#### Bugfixes

- No fork bug fixes in this release; earlier improvements are retained.

#### Maintenance

- Record relative schedule dates as an OpenSpec specification with tests for date math, matching, previews, the schedule editor and source changes.

#### Known limitations

- Experimental and off by default.
- A relative schedule cannot be the source of another relative schedule, and offsets go up to 366.
- Skipping or posting the source schedule does not skip or post relative schedules.
- If the source schedule is deleted on another device, relative schedules there update their next dates the next time they are recomputed.
- Releases published on the same day may show the "What's new" message for any of them; the Notifications page lists all.
- Synthetic staging only; no real financial data or production paperwork migration. No iPhone acceptance test is claimed.
